temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small, about ¾ lb (340 g) 400°F / 205°C · 16 min 425°F / 220°C · 20 min Medium, about 1 lb (450 g) 400°F / 205°C · 20 min 425°F / 220°C · 25 min Large, 1¼ lb (570 g) and over 400°F / 205°C · 24 min 425°F / 220°C · 30 min Dry tail, underdone middle A tenderloin tapers from a thick head to a thin tail only an inch or so across. In the air fryer the tail is cooked through long before the head, and by the time the thickest part is safe the narrow end is grey and dry. Folding the last few inches of tail back underneath the loin and tying or skewering it gives the whole piece a more even thickness. The second half of the answer is the rest. Take the tenderloin out a little short of 145°F and leave it on a board for three minutes; heat stored in the outer layers keeps moving inwards and the centre rises about 5°F while it rests. That rest is part of reaching the safe temperature, not an optional extra, and it lets the juices settle so they stay in the meat when you slice. Worked example A 1 lb tenderloin, silver skin trimmed, tail folded under, rubbed with oil, mustard and herbs. Preheat 4 minutes, cook at 400°F for 20 minutes, turning at 10. Pull it when the thick end reads about 140°F, then rest it for three minutes to reach 145°F. A small ¾ lb loin takes about 16 minutes and a large one about 24. The conventional oven equivalent is 425°F for around 25 minutes. How to tell it is done Measure in the thickest part of the head, from the side. After the three-minute rest the centre should read 145°F (63°C): blush pink, moist and safe. If it reads well above 145°F straight out of the basket, it will be firm and dry after resting, so next time take it out sooner. Slice across the grain into rounds about half an inch thick. Before it goes in Slide a thin knife under the silver skin, the shiny membrane along one side, and trim it off; it shrinks in the heat and bends the loin. Pat dry, rub with a little oil and a spice mix. If your basket is small, cut the tenderloin in half crossways rather than curling it. A sweet glaze goes on in the last few minutes. Related presets Bacon 350°F · 9 min Steak 400°F · 10 min · flip at 5 Pork chops 400°F · 12 min · flip at 6 425°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long does pork tenderloin take in the air fryer? About 20 minutes at 400°F for a 1 lb tenderloin, turned at 10 minutes, plus a three-minute rest. Small ones take around 16 minutes and large ones around 24. What temperature is pork tenderloin done at? 145°F (63°C) after a three-minute rest. Take it out about 5°F early; it rises while it rests. Why does pork tenderloin need to rest? The outside holds extra heat that keeps cooking the centre for a few minutes, and the juices settle so they stay in the slices. Should I remove the silver skin? Yes. It does not soften as it cooks and it tightens, curling the loin and making it chewy along one side. What is the equivalent in a regular oven? 425°F for around 25 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 21 minutes in a fan oven.
